# Design — Issue #1760: Fix loop condition op validation to ADR-027's eight ops

## Architectural decision summary

**Goal.** Validate `abort_when.op`, single-condition `until.op`, and every
condition's `op` in multi-condition `exit_when` at template load against the
eight-op set ADR-027 §5 specifies — `eq | neq | gt | gte | lt | lte | contains |
matches` — and implement all eight in every runtime evaluator with a refusing `*)`
branch.

**Context.** ADR-027 §5 declared the supported op set in June 2026. The engine
was partially updated: `ne` (wrong spelling) and `in` (not in ADR-027) appear in
the evaluators and load-time checks; `gt/gte/lt/lte/contains/matches` are absent.
The bug: `abort_when` has no load-time op check at all in `template.sh`, so an
unknown op silently never fires. The evaluators' missing `*)` branch means a
typo evaluates as "never matches" — the cycle runs to max_iterations with no
indication of why the predicate never fires.

**Decision.**
- **template.sh `_tpl_validate_cycles`**: add op validation for abort_when (read
  from the AW| side-channel vars already populated); add op validation for
  single-condition `until.op` (currently missing); widen multi-condition
  exit_when from `eq|ne|in` to the full eight-op set. Each check emits an error
  naming the loop, the field, the bad op, and the valid set, then returns 1.
- **cycle-orchestrator.sh `_cycle_load_template`**: widen multi-condition
  exit_when check from `eq|ne` to the eight-op set; widen single-condition until
  check from `eq|ne` to the eight-op set; add abort_when op check (currently
  absent).
- **cycle-orchestrator.sh evaluators** (`_cycle_eval_one_condition`,
  `_cycle_check_until`, `_cycle_check_abort_when`): rename `ne` to `neq`;
  remove `in`; add `gt|gte|lt|lte|contains|matches` with numeric guards on the
  numeric ops; add a `*)` branch that emits an error and returns 1.
- **ADR-027**: add `## Enforced by` section naming the enforcement tests;
  remove ADR-027 from `config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt`.

No new public surface is introduced. All changes are confined to two existing
engine files. The valid op `eq` is unchanged everywhere; all existing templates
and tests use only `eq` and are unaffected.

```scope
core/pipeline/template.sh
core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
docs/adr/ADR-027-recursive-flow-template-format.md
config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt
tests/unit/template-loader-recursive-flow-test.sh
tests/integration/cycle-orchestrator-abort-when-test.sh
tests/integration/cycle-abort-when-no-match-converges-test.sh
tests/unit/core-pipeline-cycle-events-test.sh
```

```acceptance
SPEC-1[code]: abort_when.op outside the eight-op set is refused at template load with an error naming the loop, field, bad op, and valid set covers: R-1
SPEC-2[code]: single-condition until.op outside the eight-op set is refused at template load covers: R-1
SPEC-3[code]: multi-condition exit_when op outside the eight-op set is refused at template load covers: R-1
SPEC-4[code]: the full eight-op set evaluates correctly in the exit_when single-condition evaluator (_cycle_check_until) covers: R-1
SPEC-5[code]: the full eight-op set evaluates correctly in the exit_when multi-condition evaluator (_cycle_eval_one_condition) covers: R-1
SPEC-6[code]: the full eight-op set evaluates correctly in the abort_when evaluator (_cycle_check_abort_when) covers: R-1
SPEC-7[code]: gt/gte/lt/lte with a non-numeric operand emits an error (not silent false) in each evaluator covers: R-1
SPEC-8[code]: each evaluator's *) branch returns 1 on an unrecognized op rather than silently skipping covers: R-1
SPEC-9[no-code]: ADR-027 §5 gains an ## Enforced by section naming the test files that enforce the eight-op set; ADR-027 is removed from config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt covers: R-1
WIRING:
core/pipeline/template.sh
core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh
TESTFILES:
SPEC-1: tests/unit/template-loader-recursive-flow-test.sh
SPEC-2: tests/unit/template-loader-recursive-flow-test.sh
SPEC-3: tests/unit/template-loader-recursive-flow-test.sh
SPEC-4: tests/integration/cycle-abort-when-no-match-converges-test.sh
SPEC-5: tests/integration/cycle-abort-when-no-match-converges-test.sh
SPEC-6: tests/integration/cycle-orchestrator-abort-when-test.sh
SPEC-7: tests/unit/core-pipeline-cycle-events-test.sh
SPEC-8: tests/unit/core-pipeline-cycle-events-test.sh
SPEC-9: tests/unit/template-loader-recursive-flow-test.sh
```

## Findings

**Plan scope is complete.** No files outside the seed scope pin the old op set.
Existing tests all use `op: eq` (remains valid); the golden files reference
`op=eq` (unchanged). `tests/unit/core-pipeline-template-cycles-test.sh` pins
`until.op=eq` (line 65) — `eq` stays valid, so that test is unaffected and does
not need to be in scope.

**`ne` and `in` are removed.** Neither spelling appears in any shipped template
(`config/templates/`). `ne` appears only in the evaluators and load-time checks
in the two engine files; `in` appears only in those evaluators (added via #1987,
never declared in ADR-027). No template or test fixture uses them.

**abort_when load-time op check is entirely new.** The AW| row handler in
`template.sh` stores the op into `_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_<safe>` but
`_tpl_validate_cycles` never reads it for validation. The fix adds a check there
(after the exit_when/until validation block).

**cycle-orchestrator.sh `_cycle_load_template` has no abort_when op check.** The
`_cycle_load_template` function validates the abort_when stage membership
implicitly (through _CYCLE_STAGES) but does not validate the op field. Adding it
mirrors the exit_when pattern already in that function.

**No event-schema changes.** The reason tokens (`until_op_invalid`,
`exit_when_op_invalid`) are already in use; no new event types are needed. An
`abort_when_op_invalid` reason token is a natural addition but requires no schema
entry (the `cycle.config.invalid` event type is already registered).

# Integration: ADR-027 abort_when predicate semantics (Wave 17-B, #703).
#
# abort_when (optional) is a predicate that, when matched, terminates the
# pipeline: the loop returns 1, ends with outcome aborted and reason
# cycle_abort, and records the abort word `cycle_abort` (ADR-025), which every
# enclosing cycle and the runner read on their way out. Distinct from a SIGINT
# abort (word sigint) and from blocked (outcome interrupted, no abort word).
#
# #1850 (ADR-054 §4): this used to be a new rc class, rc=6. No rc carries the
# reason any more — the word does.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
print_test_header "cycle-orchestrator — abort_when (ADR-027 / Wave 17-B)"
setup_test_env "cycle-orch-abortwhen"

source "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"

STATE_FILE="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
: > "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"

jq -n '{schema_version:1, stage_statuses:{}, updated_at:"seed"}' > "$STATE_FILE"

ABORT_TPL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/abort.yaml"
cat > "$ABORT_TPL" <<'EOF'
id: abort-test
name: abort_when test
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

flow:
  - bt_cycle

bt_cycle:
  type: cycle
  flow:
    - build
    - test
  exit_when:
    stage: test
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: pass
  abort_when:
    stage: test
    field: verdict
    op: eq
    value: corrupt
  max_iterations: 5
  on_max: continue

build:
  roles: [builder]

test:
  roles: [tester]
EOF

# Mock: build always passes; test returns "corrupt" on iter 1 (trigger abort).
cycle_dispatch_stage() {
    local stage="$1" iter="$2"
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass"
    _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="complete"
    case "$stage" in
        build) _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="pass" ;;
        test)  _CYCLE_DISPATCH_VERDICT="corrupt"
               _CYCLE_DISPATCH_STATUS="failed"
               return 1
               ;;
    esac

_TPL_CYCLES=()

load_template "$ABORT_TPL"; rc=$?
set -e
assert_eq "T1: template loads rc=0" "0" "$rc"

set +e
cycle_orchestrator_run "bt_cycle" "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$STATE_FILE"
rc=$?
set -e

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tests: cycle-* event registrations in config/event-schema.json (ADR-021, #512)
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"
print_test_header "cycle events — schema registrations (ADR-021)"
setup_test_env "cycle-events"

SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"

# All cycle events that MUST be registered per ADR-021 §Event-schema additions
required_events=(
    "cycle.start"
    "cycle.complete"
    "cycle.plateau"
    "cycle.divergence"
    "cycle.iteration.complete"
    "cycle.aborted"
    "cycle.config.invalid"
    "cycle.iteration.verdict_missing"
    "cycle.history.lost"
    "cycle.metric.invalid"
    "cycle.plateau.skipped"
    "cycle.iter.stale_artifact"
)

for ev in "${required_events[@]}"; do
    if jq -e --arg t "$ev" '.known_types | index($t)' "$SCHEMA" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_pass "event registered: $ev"
    else
        assert_fail "event registered: $ev" "missing from known_types"
    fi
done

# SPEC-3: the cycle.feedback.* events are retired with template feedback wires
# (ADR-055 §4, amended 2026-10-12) and are no longer registered.
for ev in cycle.feedback.missing cycle.feedback.absent; do
    if jq -e --arg t "$ev" '.known_types | index($t)' "$SCHEMA" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        assert_fail "[SPEC-3] retired $ev is not registered" "still in known_types"
    else
        assert_pass "[SPEC-3] retired $ev is not registered"
    fi
done

print_test_results

3	# ║  zBuild test-helpers — Shared test harness for all unit tests        ║
4	# ║  Source this from any *-test.sh file to get assert_*, setup, teardown    ║
5	# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
9	#   source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/test-helpers.sh"
10	#
11	# Provides:
12	#   Colors, counters, assert_pass/fail/eq/contains/contains_regex/gt/json_key
13	#   setup_test_env / cleanup_test_env  (temp dir, mock PATH, mock HOME)
14	#   print_test_header / print_test_results
15	#   Mock helpers: mock_binary, mock_jq, mock_git, mock_gh, mock_claude
16	
17	[[ -n "${_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
18	_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED=1
19	
20	# ─── Re-entrancy guard (#971): refuse a test invoked inside another test run ──
21	# Every *-test.sh sources this file first, so this is the universal chokepoint.
22	# A test executed from WITHIN another test run — e.g. the ablation negctl/
23	# reachability gates run `bash <changed-test>` directly — would re-enter the gate
24	# logic and fork-bomb the pipeline test stage (the recurring #929/#983/#971 class).
25	# The #983 guard in run-tests.sh only catches run-tests.sh-mediated nesting; the
26	# ablation's direct `bash` bypasses it. This guard catches BOTH paths.
27	# The sentinel has NO leading underscore so env-scrub's ^(ZBUILD_|_TPL_) clears it
28	# at every fresh-user-shell boundary (the pipeline test stage), avoiding a stale-
29	# value false refusal. Fixture-isolated nested runs set ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR and are
30	# exempt (mirrors the #983 guard's exemption). The guard fires ONLY when $0 is a
31	# `*-test.sh` being EXECUTED (`bash <test>.sh` — the ablation/fork-bomb path), not
32	# when a script merely sources this file for introspection (`bash -c "source …"`,
33	# where $0 is `bash`) — so test-helpers' own self-tests are unaffected.
34	if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE:-}" && -z "${ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR:-}" && "${0##*/}" == *-test.sh ]]; then
35	    echo "test-helpers.sh: refusing nested test invocation (re-entrancy guard #971)" >&2
36	    exit 2
37	fi
38	export ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE=1
39	
40	# The vision admission gate (ADR-049 / #1360) enforces a conforming vision doc by
41	# default. Fixture-based tests spin up temp repos with no vision doc and are not
42	# testing vision, so they must opt out — same hermeticity precedent as
43	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR. Tests that DO exercise the gate set the mode inline
44	# per-case, which overrides this default. Real (non-test) runs never source this
45	# file, so dogfood-on-zbuild still enforces against the real .zbuild/vision.md.
46	export ZBUILD_VISION_GATE="${ZBUILD_VISION_GATE:-off}"

50	GREEN='\033[38;2;74;222;128m'
51	RED='\033[38;2;248;113;113m'
52	# shellcheck disable=SC2034

54	# shellcheck disable=SC2034
55	PURPLE='\033[38;2;168;85;247m'
56	DIM='\033[2m'
57	BOLD='\033[1m'

61	PASS=0
62	FAIL=0
63	TOTAL=0
64	SKIP=0
65	FAILURES=()
66

68	# Many test files use TEST_TEMP_DIR in their setup_env() without calling
69	# setup_test_env(). Auto-create a temp dir so $TEST_TEMP_DIR is never empty.
70	# Save originals now so cleanup_test_env() can always restore them.
71	ORIG_HOME="${HOME}"

121	# ─── Master trap — kills children, calls hook, removes auto temp dir ─────────
122	# _HARNESS_SIGNAL: set by dedicated INT/TERM wrappers before calling cleanup,
123	# so _test_harness_cleanup can re-raise and exit 128+signal instead of
124	# returning into the interrupted test body (which would produce bogus failures).
125	# _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP: idempotency guard — prevents double cleanup when both
126	# a signal handler and the EXIT trap would otherwise call the body.
127	_HARNESS_SIGNAL=""
128	_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=0

130	_test_harness_cleanup() {
131	    [[ "${_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
132	    _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=1
133	    _kill_test_children
134	    _test_cleanup_hook
135	    if [[ -n "${AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -d "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
136	        rm -rf "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR"
137	    fi
138	    # Wave 19-L (#749): rm each named TEST_TEMP_DIR setup_test_env created
139	    # so tests that forgot _test_cleanup_hook / cleanup_test_env stop
140	    # leaking. Path-prefix guard against accidental rm-rf-/: each tracked
141	    # path must live under the source-time tmp-root captured in
142	    # _ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT. Using the CURRENT $TMPDIR would fail when tests
143	    # re-export TMPDIR (Copilot review #751); the source-time root is
144	    # stable for the process lifetime since AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR was created
145	    # there. (mktemp -d always returns an absolute path so the prefix
146	    # check is meaningful.)
147	    local _trk
148	    for _trk in "${_TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
149	        [[ -z "$_trk" ]] && continue
150	        [[ "$_trk" == "$_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT"/* ]] || continue
151	        [[ -d "$_trk" ]] && rm -rf "$_trk" 2>/dev/null || true
152	    done
153	    # Signal-triggered teardown: clear both the signal trap and EXIT so the
154	    # re-raised signal exits with 128+N (143/130) without running EXIT again.
155	    if [[ -n "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL:-}" ]]; then
156	        trap - "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" EXIT
157	        kill -"${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" $$
158	    fi
159	}

161	# Thin wrappers installed for TERM and INT: record the in-flight signal name
162	# then call the shared cleanup body. The cleanup body re-raises at the tail
163	# so the process exits 128+signal instead of returning into the test body.
164	_harness_signal_handler() {

179	assert_pass() {
180	    local desc="$1"
181	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
182	    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
183	    # #600: ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET=1 suppresses per-assertion echoes to keep the
184	    # pipeline test-stage banner compact. Counters still update; assert_fail
185	    # is intentionally NOT gated (failures always surface).
186	    [[ "${ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
187	    echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${RESET} ${desc}"
188	}

190	assert_fail() {
191	    local desc="$1"
192	    local detail="${2:-}"
193	    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
194	    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
195	    FAILURES[${#FAILURES[@]}]="$desc"
196	    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET} ${desc}"
197	    # An `if`, not `[[ … ]] && …` as the last line: with no detail that returned
198	    # 1, and under `set -e` the file stopped at its first failure — every later
199	    # assertion went unmeasured (#2234; 13 SPECs on #1835).
200	    if [[ -n "$detail" ]]; then echo -e "    ${DIM}${detail}${RESET}"; fi
201	    return 0
202	}

429	# ─── Reserved test identity (#1921 follow-up) ───────────────────────────────
430	# Tests used real issue numbers as identity fixtures — 25 of the 29 in use were
431	# live issues or PRs, and #42 is still OPEN. A run keyed to one of those writes
432	# fabricated prior work onto that issue's state branch; measured on this repo,
433	# zbuild/state/issue-999 held 68 commits of test payloads and issue-698 held 121.
434	# Now that CI chains and pushes (#1970, #2006), that reaches origin.
435	#
436	# 9_0000000+ is unreachable: this repo is ~2000 issues in. A stray
437	# zbuild/state/issue-9xxxxxxx ref is therefore unmistakably test residue, safe to
438	# reclaim, and can never be confused with someone's work.
439	# The floor of the reserved range. Read by lint-test-identity and the hygiene
440	# test; zb_test_issue composes its ids to always land at or above it.
441	ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR=90000000
442	export ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR
443	
444	# Sequential within a test file: 90000001, 90000002, … Files repeat the same ids,
445	# which is safe because each runs in its own throwaway repo — and if one ever
446	# escapes, the number identifies it instantly.
447	# The counter lives in a FILE, not a shell variable: callers use $(zb_test_issue),
448	# which runs in a subshell, so an in-memory counter would never advance and every
449	# call would return the same id.
450	#
451	# The id is keyed on the PID so two test files running in PARALLEL never mint the
452	# same one. They otherwise all start at 90000001, and the teardown below deletes
453	# refs from the SHARED checkout — so one file's cleanup could delete a ref another
454	# file was still asserting on. The unit tier is parallel by default (#984), and
455	# more cores make that likelier, which is why it showed on Linux CI first.
456	#
457	# Shape: 9 + PID%1000 (3) + seq (4) — always 8 digits, always >= 90000000.
458	zb_test_issue() {
459	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
460	    local f="$dir/.zb-test-issue-seq"
461	    local n=0
462	    [[ -r "$f" ]] && n="$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || printf '0')"
463	    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
464	    n=$(( n + 1 ))
465	    printf '%d' "$n" > "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
466	    local id
467	    id="$(printf '9%03d%04d' "$(( $$ % 1000 ))" "$n")"
468	    # Record it, so teardown removes exactly the refs THIS file minted rather
469	    # than every reserved ref it happens to find.
470	    printf '%s\n' "$id" >> "$dir/.zb-test-issue-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
471	    printf '%s' "$id"
472	}

474	# Goal fixtures get the same treatment: the marker makes zbuild/state/goal-<hash>
475	# traceable back to a test even though the hash itself is opaque.
476	#
477	# The hash is RECORDED as it is handed out, exactly as zb_test_issue records ids.
478	# Without that, goal refs had no teardown and no guard — which is precisely how
479	# the leak fixed in this branch survived a full identity sweep unnoticed. The
480	# derivation mirrors zbuild_goal_key: sha256 of the text with all whitespace
481	# stripped, truncated to 12 hex.
482	zb_test_goal() {
483	    local text; text="$(printf '[zb-test] %s' "${1:-fixture}")"
484	    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
485	    local h
486	    h="$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr -d '[:space:]' | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-12)"
487	    printf '%s\n' "$h" >> "$dir/.zb-test-goal-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
488	    printf '%s' "$text"
489	}

509	# Reserved-range state refs in a repo (default: the real checkout). Used by both
510	# the teardown below and the suite-wide hygiene guard.
511	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # callers live in tests/, which CI's shellcheck step
512	# does not scan (it covers scripts core plugins), so the optional repo argument
513	# looks unpassed from inside this file alone.
514	zb_test_reserved_refs() {
515	    local repo="${1:-${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}}"
516	    # Prefix glob, then a NUMERIC filter — not 'issue-9???????'. That counted
517	    # characters, so it covered 90000000-99999999 only, while lint-test-identity
518	    # and _cleanup_issue_ref_decision both gate on >= 90000000. An id above the
519	    # 8-digit range would have passed both and been invisible here.
520	    local _ref _n
521	    while IFS= read -r _ref; do
522	        [[ -n "$_ref" ]] || continue
523	        _n="${_ref##*/issue-}"
524	        [[ "$_n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
525	        # An explicit if, not `[[ … ]] && printf`: the && form returns non-zero
526	        # when the test is false, and as the last command in the loop body that
527	        # aborts callers running under `set -e`.

621	# Install an envelope-aware mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
622	# Branches on argv: when invoked with `--output-format json` (ADR-018 Pattern 1
623	# decision #8, #476), wraps the payload in a {type:result,result:...} envelope
624	# so the router's `.result` extraction finds it. Otherwise emits the payload
625	# as raw text (legacy text-mode callers).
626	#
627	# Usage:
628	#   install_envelope_mock_claude <payload>                        # payload is inline text
629	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --file <payload_file>            # payload comes from a file at call time
630	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-argv <path> <payload>   # also record argv to <path>
631	#   install_envelope_mock_claude --record-prompt <path> <payload> # also record `-p <prompt>` to <path>
632	#
633	# Flags may be combined (e.g. --file + --record-argv).
634	install_envelope_mock_claude() {
635	    local payload="" payload_file="" argv_record="" prompt_record=""
636	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
637	        case "$1" in
638	            --file)          payload_file="$2"; shift 2 ;;
639	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
640	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
641	            *)               payload="$1"; shift ;;
642	        esac
643	    done
644	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
645	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
646	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
647	#!/usr/bin/env bash
648	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude (#476).
649	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
650	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
651	fi
652	envelope_mode=0
653	prompt_text=""
654	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
655	    case "\$1" in
656	        --output-format|json) envelope_mode=1; shift ;;
657	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
658	        *)  shift ;;
659	    esac
660	done
661	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
662	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
663	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
664	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
665	fi
666	if [[ -n "${payload_file:-}" ]]; then
667	    payload="\$(cat "$payload_file")"
668	else
669	    payload=$(printf '%q' "$payload")
670	fi
671	if [[ \$envelope_mode -eq 1 ]]; then
672	    jq -n --arg r "\$payload" '{type:"result",subtype:"success",result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
673	else
674	    printf '%s\n' "\$payload"
675	fi
676	exit 0
677	MOCK
678	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
679	}

681	# Install an envelope-aware ERROR mock claude binary on PATH ($TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin).
682	# Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude but simulates a failed `claude` run that
683	# still prints a JSON result envelope to stdout and exits non-zero — the exact
684	# shape route.sh persists to its diagnostic sidecar
685	# (${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-…/artifacts}/stage-io/<stage>-sync-error.raw-claude-output.json).
686	#
687	# The default envelope simulates the #1052 dogfood failure: the planner burned
688	# all its turns exploring the repo and hit max_turns before emitting plan.json:
689	#   {"type":"result","subtype":"error_max_turns","is_error":true,
690	#    "num_turns":<N>,"result":"<partial reasoning text>",
691	#    "usage":{input_tokens:…,output_tokens:…}}
692	# then `exit 1`.
693	#
694	# Everything is tunable via env vars read AT MOCK-INVOCATION TIME (not install
695	# time), so a test can export a different value just before calling plan_run and
696	# the same installed binary honors it. This lets one installer cover three cases:
697	#   (a) max_turns exhaustion (defaults).
698	#   (b) a non-max_turns crash — set ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE to e.g. "error" and the
699	#       discriminator (subtype != error_max_turns) stays on the
700	#       claude_cli_failed path.
701	#   (c) a max_turns envelope whose .result IS a valid plan.json — set
702	#       ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT to the plan JSON; recovery should salvage it.
703	#
704	# Env vars (all optional):
705	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE    envelope .subtype     (default: error_max_turns)
706	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS  envelope .num_turns   (default: 25)
707	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT     envelope .result      (default: a partial-reasoning blurb)
708	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_RC         process exit code     (default: 1)
709	#   ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR   envelope .is_error    (default: true)
710	#
711	# Usage:
712	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error                       # max_turns defaults
713	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-argv <path>  # also record argv
714	#   install_envelope_mock_claude_error --record-prompt <path> # also record -p prompt
715	#
716	# Flags may be combined. Mirrors install_envelope_mock_claude's recording hooks
717	# so resume/dogfood tests can assert the captured prompt across runs.
718	install_envelope_mock_claude_error() {
719	    local argv_record="" prompt_record=""
720	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
721	        case "$1" in
722	            --record-argv)   argv_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
723	            --record-prompt) prompt_record="$2"; shift 2 ;;
724	            *)               shift ;;
725	        esac
726	    done
727	    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
728	    local mock_bin="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/claude"
729	    cat > "$mock_bin" <<MOCK
730	#!/usr/bin/env bash
731	# Auto-generated by install_envelope_mock_claude_error (#1052).
732	if [[ -n "${argv_record:-}" ]]; then
733	    printf '%s\n' "\$@" > "$argv_record"
734	fi
735	prompt_text=""
736	while [[ \$# -gt 0 ]]; do
737	    case "\$1" in
738	        -p) prompt_text="\${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
739	        *)  shift ;;
740	    esac
741	done
742	# The router sends the prompt on stdin (#1849: argv overflowed at 128 KiB).
743	[[ -n "\$prompt_text" ]] || prompt_text="\$(cat)"
744	if [[ -n "${prompt_record:-}" ]]; then
745	    printf '%s' "\$prompt_text" > "$prompt_record"
746	fi
747	# Tunable envelope fields — read at invocation time so a test can vary the
748	# shape per call without reinstalling the mock.
749	_subtype="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_SUBTYPE:-error_max_turns}"
750	_num_turns="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_NUM_TURNS:-25}"
751	_is_error="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_IS_ERROR:-true}"
752	_rc="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RC:-1}"
753	_result="\${ZBUILD_MOCK_RESULT:-Explored core/ and plugins/ but ran out of turns before emitting a complete plan. Partial findings: the change touches the router and the plan plugin.}"
754	jq -n \\
755	    --arg st "\$_subtype" \\
756	    --argjson nt "\$_num_turns" \\
757	    --argjson ie "\$_is_error" \\
758	    --arg r "\$_result" \\
759	    '{type:"result",subtype:\$st,is_error:\$ie,num_turns:\$nt,result:\$r,usage:{input_tokens:0,output_tokens:0},tool_uses:[]}'
760	exit "\$_rc"
761	MOCK
762	    chmod +x "$mock_bin"
763	}

767	# Fail loudly on an unknown platform argument. A typo (e.g. `lniux`) must NOT
768	# silently skip a test forever while still reporting success — that would let CI
769	# mask a test that never runs. Exits non-zero so the mistake surfaces.

785	    case "$current" in
786	        Darwin) current="macos" ;;
787	        Linux)  current="linux" ;;
788	    esac

1031	#   zb_test_work_procs <trace_file>  the subshells it ran in besides this one
1032	# <cmd>'s output is discarded; run it again for its answer.

1053	# ─── zb_test_kill_tree <pid> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
1054	# KILL <pid> and every process under it. KILL cannot be caught, so a runner
1055	# killed alone cleans up nothing: its forked stage and the stage's time-limit
1056	# watchdog (copies of its shell, so they show as runner.sh) ran on, the watchdog
1057	# for up to the stage's limit.
1058	#
1059	# Deepest first, so no parent dies before its children (a child whose parent is
1060	# gone is re-parented away and can no longer be found), and read again until
1061	# nothing is left, for a child forked while the tree was being read. Nothing is
1062	# STOPped on the way: a stopped process whose parent dies leaves an orphaned
1063	# process group with a stopped member, and the kernel hangs up that whole group
1064	# — on macOS CI, the test's own. A process already gone is no error, under
1065	# set -e too: an abort test's runner has usually exited on its TERM by then.
1066	_zb_test_tree() { local c; printf '%s\n' "$1"; for c in $(pgrep -P "$1" 2>/dev/null || true); do _zb_test_tree "$c"; done; }
1067	zb_test_kill_tree() {
1068	    local -a t
1069	    local i r
1070	    for (( r = 0; r < 5; r++ )); do
1071	        mapfile -t t < <(_zb_test_tree "$1")
1072	        for (( i = ${#t[@]} - 1; i >= 0; i-- )); do kill -KILL "${t[i]}" 2>/dev/null || true; done
1073	        kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null || (( ${#t[@]} > 1 )) || break
1074	    done
1075	    return 0
1076	}

1078	# Bounded poll for a grep pattern to appear in an events/state file (#619's
1079	# "wait-for-event-content" pattern; reused by #887/#1127/#1149). Replaces the
1080	# anti-pattern of a fixed `sleep N` followed by a single-shot read of an
1081	# event/state file — that races a slow CI box (the writer may not have flushed
1082	# the line yet). This polls the file until the content appears, bounded by a
1083	# generous timeout so a genuinely-never-emitted event still fails fast-enough
1084	# instead of hanging.
1085	#
1086	# Usage: wait_for_event <file> <grep_pattern> [max_iters=600] [interval=0.1]
1087	#   - <grep_pattern> is a basic-regex passed to `grep -q` (quote JSON fragments,
1088	#     e.g. '"pipeline.start"').
1089	#   - Default bound: 600 × 0.1s = 60s — generous enough for a loaded shared CI
1090	#     runner, short enough to never wedge the suite.
1091	# Returns 0 as soon as the pattern is present; 1 if the bound elapses first.
1092	# Does NOT assert — callers decide whether a timeout is fatal so the failure
1093	# message stays test-specific.
1094	wait_for_event() {
1095	    local file="$1" pattern="$2" max_iters="${3:-600}" interval="${4:-0.1}" i
1096	    for (( i = 0; i < max_iters; i++ )); do
1097	        if [[ -f "$file" ]] && grep -q "$pattern" "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
1098	            return 0
1099	        fi
1100	        sleep "$interval"
1101	    done
1102	    return 1
1103	}

1128	# ─── setup_git_temp_repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1129	# Creates a real, minimal git repo under $TEST_TEMP_DIR/<name> with one
1130	# initial commit. Returns its absolute path on stdout. Used by integration
1131	# tests that exercise real `git checkout`/`git symbolic-ref` against an
1132	# isolated repo (issue #484).
1133	#
1134	# Usage:
1135	#   repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo myrepo)"
1136	#   (cd "$repo" && some_test)
1137	setup_git_temp_repo() {
1138	    local name="${1:-gitrepo}"
1139	    local repo="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name"
1140	    mkdir -p "$repo" 2>/dev/null || return 1
1141	    (
1142	        # #2103 / ADR-024: the cd MUST be fatal. `set -e` is inert inside this
1143	        # subshell because its status is tested by `|| return 1` below, so a
1144	        # failed cd would otherwise run every git command in the CALLER'S
1145	        # checkout — which is exactly what committed seed.txt into a real
1146	        # worktree and pushed a branch to the real origin on 2026-09-15.
1147	        cd "$repo" || exit 1
1148	        # Use the real git binary (not whatever PATH shim may be present).
1149	        local real_git
1150	        real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)"
1151	        # If a shim like the parity-fixture mock is on PATH, fall back to
1152	        # well-known absolute locations.
1153	        if [[ -z "$real_git" ]]; then
1154	            for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
1155	                [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
1156	            done
1157	        fi
1158	        [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && return 1
1159	        "$real_git" init -q -b main 2>/dev/null || "$real_git" init -q
1160	        "$real_git" config user.email "test@zbuild.local"
1161	        "$real_git" config user.name "zbuild-test"
1162	        "$real_git" config commit.gpgsign false
1163	        echo "seed" > seed.txt
1164	        "$real_git" add seed.txt
1165	        "$real_git" commit -q -m "seed"
1166	        # Normalize default branch name to 'main' for predictable tests.
1167	        local cur
1168	        cur="$("$real_git" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
1169	        if [[ "$cur" != "main" ]]; then
1170	            "$real_git" branch -m "$cur" main 2>/dev/null || true
1171	        fi
1172	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1173	    printf '%s\n' "$repo"
1174	}

1176	# ── setup_git_master_origin (#2103) ──────────────────────────────────────────
1177	# A bare origin whose default branch is `master` (not `main`), seeded with one
1178	# commit, plus a working clone of it whose origin/HEAD → origin/master. Prints
1179	# the clone's path; prints nothing and returns 1 on any setup failure. Extracted
1180	# from tests/integration/intake-branch-ahead-count-test.sh, where a failed seed
1181	# clone let the seeding subshell run — and `git push origin HEAD:master` — in
1182	# the caller's checkout against the caller's origin. Every cd here is fatal
1183	# because each subshell's status is tested (see setup_git_temp_repo).
1184	#
1185	# Usage:
1186	#   clone="$(setup_git_master_origin a)" || fail "setup"
1187	setup_git_master_origin() {
1188	    local label="${1:-m}"
1189	    local bare="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bare-${label}.git"
1190	    local work="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/work-${label}"
1191	    local tmp_init="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/init-${label}"
1192	
1193	    git init --bare "$bare" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1194	    git -C "$bare" symbolic-ref HEAD "refs/heads/master" 2>/dev/null || { printf ''; return 1; }
1195	
1196	    # Seed via a throwaway clone. The clone's OWN rc is checked before the
1197	    # subshell so a clone failure never reaches the cd; the cd is fatal anyway.
1198	    git clone "$bare" "$tmp_init" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1199	    (
1200	        cd "$tmp_init" || exit 1
1201	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1202	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1203	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1204	        # Unborn HEAD: -b names the branch regardless of init.defaultBranch.
1205	        git checkout -q -b master 2>/dev/null || git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/master || exit 1
1206	        echo "seed" > seed.txt || exit 1
1207	        git add seed.txt || exit 1
1208	        git commit -q -m "seed" || exit 1
1209	        git push -q origin HEAD:"refs/heads/master" || exit 1
1210	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1211	    rm -rf "$tmp_init"
1212	
1213	    # The bare repo MUST now carry master; a bare `.git` check downstream cannot
1214	    # tell "seeded" from "empty", and an unborn HEAD makes `checkout master` a no-op.
1215	    git -C "$bare" show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/master || { printf ''; return 1; }
1216	
1217	    git clone "$bare" "$work" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1218	    (
1219	        cd "$work" || exit 1
1220	        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
1221	        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
1222	        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
1223	    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
1224	
1225	    printf '%s\n' "$work"
1226	}

1228	# ── install_template_overlay (#1270) ─────────────────────────────────────────
1229	# Copy one or more template fixtures into a repo's per-repo override dir
1230	# (<repo>/.zbuild/templates/<id>.yaml), the generic ADR-016 overlay seam. A test
1231	# that then runs the engine with CWD = <repo> resolves the fixture WITHOUT any
1232	# env var and WITHOUT writing into the tracked config/templates/ — the overlay
1233	# lives entirely inside the test's temp repo (reaped by the master EXIT/INT/TERM
1234	# trap). This replaces the #1268 ZBUILD_TEMPLATES_DIR seam (reverted in #1270):
1235	# no ambient env, no global state; hermeticity comes from CWD isolation.
1236	#
1237	# Each fixture is a `.zbuild/templates/` overlay, so it MUST carry `extends: <id>`
1238	# (ADR-016). The shipped base it extends (usually `simple`) is read from the
1239	# engine tree unchanged — only the overlay id needs a fixture.
1240	#
1241	# Usage: install_template_overlay <repo> <id> [<id> ...]
1242	# install_simple_loop_continue <repo> — overlay template `simple-loop-continue`:
1243	# the shipped simple.yaml with delivery_loop set to on_max: continue.
1244	# #2241: simple.yaml's outer loop is on_max: halt, and the runner honours it.
1245	# Tests whose subject is the CONTINUE path past an exhausted loop (#766, #1217)
1246	# drive this instead — generated from the real template at test time, so it
1247	# never drifts from it. (#2369: the design loop it once also changed is retired.)
1248	install_simple_loop_continue() {
1249	    local _repo="${1:?install_simple_loop_continue: <repo> required}" _src_root
1250	    _src_root="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)"
1251	    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
1252	    awk '
1253	        /^id: simple$/ { print "id: simple-loop-continue"; print "extends: simple"; next }
1254	        /^delivery_loop:/ { in_dl = 1; print; next }
1255	        in_dl && /^[a-z_-]+:/ { in_dl = 0 }
1256	        in_dl && /^  on_max: halt$/ { print "  on_max: continue"; next }
1257	        { print }
1258	    ' "$_src_root/config/templates/simple.yaml" > "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml"
1259	    grep -q '^id: simple-loop-continue$' "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml" || return 1
1260	    # Committed, as install_template_overlay_committed does: an untracked
1261	    # overlay leaves the tree dirty and intake refuses to start on it.
1262	    local _git; _git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
1263	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" add .zbuild/templates >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1264	    "$_git" -C "$_repo" commit -q -m "add test template overlay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
1265	}

1267	install_template_overlay() {
1268	    local _repo="$1"; shift
1269	    # Fail fast on an empty repo arg (e.g. an unset OVERLAY_REPO): otherwise we'd
1270	    # mkdir/cp into /.zbuild/templates and fail later with a confusing error.
1271	    if [[ -z "$_repo" ]]; then
1272	        echo "install_template_overlay: <repo> argument required (got empty)" >&2
1273	        return 1
1274	    fi
1275	    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
1276	    # The overlay is test setup, not work: kept out of `git status` so the
1277	    # engine's dirty-tree check (#2367) does not refuse the run.
1278	    if [[ -d "$_repo/.git/info" ]] && ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
1279	        printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_repo/.git/info/exclude"
1280	    fi
1281	    # Repo root derived from THIS helper's location (…/scripts/lib → repo root),
1282	    # not the caller's cwd, so it resolves regardless of where the test runs.
1283	    local _hdir _src_root
1284	    _hdir="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
1285	    _src_root="$(cd "$_hdir/../.." && pwd)"
1286	    local _id _src
1287	    for _id in "$@"; do
1288	        _src="$_src_root/tests/fixtures/templates/${_id}.yaml"
1289	        if [[ ! -f "$_src" ]]; then
1290	            echo "install_template_overlay: fixture not found: $_src" >&2
1291	            return 1
1292	        fi
1293	        cp "$_src" "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/${_id}.yaml"
1294	    done
1295	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  zBuild test-helpers — Shared test harness for all unit tests        ║
# ║  Source this from any *-test.sh file to get assert_*, setup, teardown    ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Usage:
#   SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
#   source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/test-helpers.sh"
#
# Provides:
#   Colors, counters, assert_pass/fail/eq/contains/contains_regex/gt/json_key
#   setup_test_env / cleanup_test_env  (temp dir, mock PATH, mock HOME)
#   print_test_header / print_test_results
#   Mock helpers: mock_binary, mock_jq, mock_git, mock_gh, mock_claude

[[ -n "${_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_TEST_HELPERS_LOADED=1

# ─── Re-entrancy guard (#971): refuse a test invoked inside another test run ──
# Every *-test.sh sources this file first, so this is the universal chokepoint.
# A test executed from WITHIN another test run — e.g. the ablation negctl/
# reachability gates run `bash <changed-test>` directly — would re-enter the gate
# logic and fork-bomb the pipeline test stage (the recurring #929/#983/#971 class).
# The #983 guard in run-tests.sh only catches run-tests.sh-mediated nesting; the
# ablation's direct `bash` bypasses it. This guard catches BOTH paths.
# The sentinel has NO leading underscore so env-scrub's ^(ZBUILD_|_TPL_) clears it
# at every fresh-user-shell boundary (the pipeline test stage), avoiding a stale-
# value false refusal. Fixture-isolated nested runs set ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR and are
# exempt (mirrors the #983 guard's exemption). The guard fires ONLY when $0 is a
# `*-test.sh` being EXECUTED (`bash <test>.sh` — the ablation/fork-bomb path), not
# when a script merely sources this file for introspection (`bash -c "source …"`,
# where $0 is `bash`) — so test-helpers' own self-tests are unaffected.
if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE:-}" && -z "${ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR:-}" && "${0##*/}" == *-test.sh ]]; then
    echo "test-helpers.sh: refusing nested test invocation (re-entrancy guard #971)" >&2
    exit 2
fi
export ZBUILD_TEST_EXEC_ACTIVE=1

# The vision admission gate (ADR-049 / #1360) enforces a conforming vision doc by
# default. Fixture-based tests spin up temp repos with no vision doc and are not
# testing vision, so they must opt out — same hermeticity precedent as
# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR. Tests that DO exercise the gate set the mode inline
# per-case, which overrides this default. Real (non-test) runs never source this
# file, so dogfood-on-zbuild still enforces against the real .zbuild/vision.md.
export ZBUILD_VISION_GATE="${ZBUILD_VISION_GATE:-off}"

# ─── Colors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CYAN='\033[38;2;0;212;255m'
GREEN='\033[38;2;74;222;128m'
RED='\033[38;2;248;113;113m'
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
YELLOW='\033[38;2;250;204;21m'
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
PURPLE='\033[38;2;168;85;247m'
DIM='\033[2m'
BOLD='\033[1m'
RESET='\033[0m'

# ─── Counters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PASS=0
FAIL=0
TOTAL=0
SKIP=0
FAILURES=()

# ─── Auto-initialize TEST_TEMP_DIR ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Many test files use TEST_TEMP_DIR in their setup_env() without calling
# setup_test_env(). Auto-create a temp dir so $TEST_TEMP_DIR is never empty.
# Save originals now so cleanup_test_env() can always restore them.
ORIG_HOME="${HOME}"
ORIG_PATH="${PATH}"
# Sandbox ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR so stage-io writes during
# tests never escape to the outer pipeline's state directory (#1713).
# `+set` records SET-ness separately from the value: `${VAR:-}` collapses "unset"
# and "set but empty" into the same "", and cleanup would then unset a variable
# the caller had deliberately exported as empty. `${VAR-}` (no colon) keeps an
# empty value as empty.
ORIG_STATE_DIR_SET="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR+set}"
ORIG_STATE_DIR="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR-}"
ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR_SET="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR+set}"
ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR-}"
# Track the auto-created temp dir separately so cleanup always removes it,
# even if individual tests later reassign TEST_TEMP_DIR in their own setup_env.
AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/zb-test-auto.XXXXXX")
TEST_TEMP_DIR="$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR"
# Wave 19-L (#751 Copilot review): freeze the tmp-root at source time so
# the master trap's prefix guard stays valid even when tests re-export
# TMPDIR (e.g., to $TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp for sandbox mktemp shims).
_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT="${_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT%/}"
mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home/.zbuild"
mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp"
# Sandbox mktemp shim — macOS plain `mktemp`/`mktemp -d` (no template) ignores
# $TMPDIR and uses /var/folders which is write-blocked in the sandbox.
# Route templateless calls through a writable directory.
# Linux mktemp respects $TMPDIR natively so no shim is needed there; installing
# one would break test setup_env() loops that do `ln -sf "$(command -v mktemp)"`
# because command -v resolves to the shim itself (same-file ln error).
if [[ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
    printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n_s="%s"\nif [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp "$_s/tmp.XXXXXX"; fi\nif [[ $# -eq 1 && "$1" == "-d" ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp -d "$_s/tmpd.XXXXXX"; fi\nexec /usr/bin/mktemp "$@"\n' \
        "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp" > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
    chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
fi
export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin:$PATH"
# ─── Child-process killer (used by master trap) ──────────────────────────────
_kill_test_children() {
    local pids
    pids=$(jobs -p 2>/dev/null) || true
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word splitting intentional to pass multiple PIDs
    [[ -n "$pids" ]] && kill $pids 2>/dev/null || true
    pkill -P $$ 2>/dev/null || true
    wait 2>/dev/null || true
}

# ─── Script-level cleanup hook — override in each test script ────────────────
# Default is a no-op; scripts set: _test_cleanup_hook() { cleanup_env; }
_test_cleanup_hook() { :; }

# ─── Master trap — kills children, calls hook, removes auto temp dir ─────────
# _HARNESS_SIGNAL: set by dedicated INT/TERM wrappers before calling cleanup,
# so _test_harness_cleanup can re-raise and exit 128+signal instead of
# returning into the interrupted test body (which would produce bogus failures).
# _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP: idempotency guard — prevents double cleanup when both
# a signal handler and the EXIT trap would otherwise call the body.
_HARNESS_SIGNAL=""
_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=0

_test_harness_cleanup() {
    [[ "${_HARNESS_CLEANED_UP:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
    _HARNESS_CLEANED_UP=1
    _kill_test_children
    _test_cleanup_hook
    if [[ -n "${AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -d "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -rf "$AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR"
    fi
    # Wave 19-L (#749): rm each named TEST_TEMP_DIR setup_test_env created
    # so tests that forgot _test_cleanup_hook / cleanup_test_env stop
    # leaking. Path-prefix guard against accidental rm-rf-/: each tracked
    # path must live under the source-time tmp-root captured in
    # _ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT. Using the CURRENT $TMPDIR would fail when tests
    # re-export TMPDIR (Copilot review #751); the source-time root is
    # stable for the process lifetime since AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR was created
    # there. (mktemp -d always returns an absolute path so the prefix
    # check is meaningful.)
    local _trk
    for _trk in "${_TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
        [[ -z "$_trk" ]] && continue
        [[ "$_trk" == "$_ZB_TEST_TMP_ROOT"/* ]] || continue
        [[ -d "$_trk" ]] && rm -rf "$_trk" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
    # Signal-triggered teardown: clear both the signal trap and EXIT so the
    # re-raised signal exits with 128+N (143/130) without running EXIT again.
    if [[ -n "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL:-}" ]]; then
        trap - "${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" EXIT
        kill -"${_HARNESS_SIGNAL}" $$
    fi
}

# Thin wrappers installed for TERM and INT: record the in-flight signal name
# then call the shared cleanup body. The cleanup body re-raises at the tail
# so the process exits 128+signal instead of returning into the test body.
_harness_signal_handler() {
    local _sig="$1"
    _HARNESS_SIGNAL="$_sig"
    _test_harness_cleanup
}

# Wave 19-L: initialize the tracking array (declared here so setup_test_env
# can += without `unbound variable` under set -u).
_TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS=()
trap '_test_harness_cleanup' EXIT
trap '_harness_signal_handler INT'  INT
trap '_harness_signal_handler TERM' TERM

# ─── Assertions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

assert_pass() {
    local desc="$1"
    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
    PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    # #600: ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET=1 suppresses per-assertion echoes to keep the
    # pipeline test-stage banner compact. Counters still update; assert_fail
    # is intentionally NOT gated (failures always surface).
    [[ "${ZBUILD_TEST_QUIET:-0}" == "1" ]] && return 0
    echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${RESET} ${desc}"
}

assert_fail() {
    local desc="$1"
    local detail="${2:-}"
    TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
    FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    FAILURES[${#FAILURES[@]}]="$desc"
    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET} ${desc}"
    # An `if`, not `[[ … ]] && …` as the last line: with no detail that returned
    # 1, and under `set -e` the file stopped at its first failure — every later
    # assertion went unmeasured (#2234; 13 SPECs on #1835).
    if [[ -n "$detail" ]]; then echo -e "    ${DIM}${detail}${RESET}"; fi
    return 0
}

assert_eq() {
    local desc="$1"
    local expected="$2"
    local actual="$3"
    if [[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]]; then
        assert_pass "$desc"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "expected: $expected, got: $actual"
    fi
}

assert_contains() {
    local desc="$1"
    local haystack="$2"
    local needle="$3"
    if grep -qF -- "$needle" <<< "$haystack" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "$desc"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "output missing: $needle"
    fi
}

assert_contains_regex() {
    local desc="$1"
    local haystack="$2"
    local pattern="$3"
    if grep -qE -- "$pattern" <<< "$haystack" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "$desc"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "output missing pattern: $pattern"
    fi
}

assert_gt() {
    local desc="$1"
    local actual="$2"
    local threshold="$3"
    if [[ "$actual" -gt "$threshold" ]] 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "$desc"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "expected >$threshold, got: $actual"
    fi
}

assert_json_key() {
    local desc="$1"
    local json="$2"
    local key="$3"
    local expected="$4"
    local actual
    actual=$(echo "$json" | jq -r "$key" 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]]; then
        assert_pass "$desc"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "key $key: expected $expected, got: $actual"
    fi
}

assert_exit_code() {
    local desc="$1"
    local expected="$2"
    local actual="$3"
    if [[ "$expected" == "$actual" ]]; then
        assert_pass "$desc (exit $actual)"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "expected exit code: $expected, got: $actual"
    fi
}

assert_file_exists() {
    local desc="$1"
    local filepath="$2"
    if [[ -f "$filepath" ]]; then
        assert_pass "$desc"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "file not found: $filepath"
    fi
}

assert_file_not_exists() {
    local desc="$1"
    local filepath="$2"
    if [[ ! -f "$filepath" ]]; then
        assert_pass "$desc"
    else
        assert_fail "$desc" "file should not exist: $filepath"
    fi
}

# ─── Test Environment ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ─── Which engine locations a test may share (#2252 F, #1910) ────────────────
# Every ZBUILD_* variable naming a place the engine WRITES is cleared per test,
# so it falls back to the sandboxed $HOME (below) or whatever the test sets
# after setup. The pipeline's test stage exports ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT, a cost
# ledger and a cache dir for the suite it runs; clearing only STATE_DIR and
# ARTIFACT_DIR let every test file share one stage-io folder and seq counter
# (#2032 run 36969130031). tests/unit/test-env-isolation-test.sh fails on any
# location variable the engine reads that is in neither list.
_ZB_TEST_ISOLATED_VARS=(
    ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT ZBUILD_STATE_DIR ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR ZBUILD_STATE_FILE
    ZBUILD_DATA_ROOT ZBUILD_RUN_ROOT ZBUILD_POOL_ROOT ZBUILD_SCRATCH_ROOT
    ZBUILD_WORKTREE_ROOT ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS
    ZBUILD_CYCLE_FEEDBACK_DIR ZBUILD_NEGCTL_ARTIFACT_DIR
    ZBUILD_RUN_START_MARKER ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL
    ZBUILD_MEMORY_DB ZBUILD_CACHE_DIR ZBUILD_COST_LEDGER ZBUILD_ROUTER_TOOL_USES_FILE
    ZBUILD_WIKI_ROOT ZBUILD_INSTALL_DIR ZBUILD_BIN_DIR
)
# Code, config and the test runner's own channels: read, or deliberately shared
# by run-tests.sh across files (the timing file).
_ZB_TEST_INHERITED_VARS=(
    ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT ZBUILD_PLUGINS_DIR ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR ZBUILD_CORE_DIR
    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT ZBUILD_MAIN_REPO_ROOT ZBUILD_PROJECT_ROOT
    ZBUILD_CONFIG_FILE ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE ZBUILD_DISABLED_FILE
    ZBUILD_SECRET_SCAN_ALLOWLIST_FILE ZBUILD_TESTS_DIR ZBUILD_MUTATION_DIR
    ZBUILD_TEST_TIMING_FILE ZBUILD_TEST_DURATIONS_FILE ZBUILD_DISCOVERY_MEMO_DIR ZBUILD_RELEASE_LOCAL_DIR ZBUILD_RELEASE_VERSION_FILE
)

# _zb_test_stage_blocks <dir> — the engine's three blocks for a stage that has
# no repository settings, no earlier stage and no manifest, written with the
# engine's own writers (#1799: never hand-made).
_zb_test_stage_blocks() {
    local dir="$1"
    (
        # shellcheck source=./stage-prompt.sh
        source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/stage-prompt.sh" || exit 1
        mkdir -p "$dir" "$dir/repo" "$dir/state" || exit 1
        _stage_block_from_repo test-stage "$dir/repo" > "$dir/from-repo.md"
        _stage_block_previous_work test-stage "$dir/state" "$dir/plugins" "" "$dir/repo" \
            > "$dir/previous-work.md"
        _stage_block_rules test-stage "$dir/state" "$dir/no-manifest.yaml" > "$dir/rules.md"
    ) 2>/dev/null
}

# zb_test_previous_work <state_file> <plugins_root> [consumer] — the engine's
# Previous work block a later stage receives (ADR-067 §8), from the engine's
# own writers. The flow is the caller's _TPL_STAGES.
zb_test_previous_work() {
    local state_file="$1" proot="$2" consumer="${3:-later}" sd
    sd="$(dirname "$state_file")"
    (
        # shellcheck source=./stage-prompt.sh
        source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/stage-prompt.sh" || exit 1
        declare -F _inputs_resolve_stage >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)/core/pipeline/input-resolve.sh" || exit 1
        _stage_block_previous_work "$consumer" "$sd" "$proot" \
            "$(_inputs_resolve_stage "$consumer" "$proot" "$sd")" "$sd"
    ) 2>/dev/null
}

setup_test_env() {
    local test_name="${1:-zb-test}"
    # Clean up auto-created temp dir and create a named one
    [[ -n "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" && -d "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]] && rm -rf "$TEST_TEMP_DIR"
    TEST_TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/${test_name}.XXXXXX")
    # Wave 19-L (#749): register the named TEST_TEMP_DIR for cleanup in the
    # master trap. Without this, tests that forget to set _test_cleanup_hook
    # or call cleanup_test_env leak the named dir. Audit (2026-06-08) found
    # 44 of 245 setup_test_env callsites had this gap → 1,261 leaked dirs.
    # The master trap (_test_harness_cleanup) reads _TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS
    # and rm -rf's each, in addition to AUTO_TEST_TEMP_DIR.
    _TRACKED_TEST_TEMP_DIRS+=("$TEST_TEMP_DIR")
    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home/.zbuild"
    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/project"
    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/logs"

    # ORIG_HOME/ORIG_PATH/ORIG_STATE_DIR already saved at source time.
    export HOME="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home"
    export PATH="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin:$PATH"
    # Unset ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR so any ambient pipeline
    # values do not leak into this test process (#1713). stage-io falls back to
    # ${HOME}/.zbuild/state (sandboxed above) when both are unset, landing all
    # writes in the sandbox. We unset rather than redirect to avoid perturbing
    # callers that manage their own artifact paths after setup.
    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/home/.zbuild/state"
    # #2252 F: every written location, not only STATE_DIR / ARTIFACT_DIR.
    unset "${_ZB_TEST_ISOLATED_VARS[@]}"
    # The event bus resolves its paths when it is SOURCED — usually before this
    # call, with the real $HOME — so clearing them would leave it nowhere to
    # write, and leaving them would write under the real ~/.zbuild. Point them
    # into this test's own folder; a test that wants its own sets them after.
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
    mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR"
    export NO_GITHUB=true
    export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0

    # ADR-067 §8: a stage that calls a model composes its prompt with the
    # engine's three blocks, which plugin_hook_call writes at dispatch. A test
    # that calls a stage's run function directly gets a minimal set, written by
    # the engine's own code; a test about the blocks sets its own.
    _zb_test_stage_blocks "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-blocks" \
        && export ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-blocks"

    # Prevent CI-environment leakage into the test subprocess.
    # GitHub Actions exports WORKSPACE_BRANCH and (in some workflows) CI_MODE; if
    # those leak into stage-level unit tests they silently divert intake into the
    # CI-workspace-branch path, breaking branch-creation assertions.
    unset WORKSPACE_BRANCH CI_MODE

    # Link real jq if available
    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ln -sf "$(command -v jq)" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/jq"
    fi

    # Mock timeout — macOS doesn't have GNU coreutils timeout by default
    if ! command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/timeout" <<'TIMEOUT_EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
shift  # skip the timeout duration
exec "$@"
TIMEOUT_EOF
        chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/timeout"
    fi

    # Sandbox mktemp shim — macOS only (see auto-init comment above for rationale).
    mkdir -p "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp"
    if [[ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
        printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n_s="%s"\nif [[ $# -eq 0 ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp "$_s/tmp.XXXXXX"; fi\nif [[ $# -eq 1 && "$1" == "-d" ]]; then exec /usr/bin/mktemp -d "$_s/tmpd.XXXXXX"; fi\nexec /usr/bin/mktemp "$@"\n' \
            "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/_tmp" > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
        chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/mktemp"
    fi
}

# ─── Reserved test identity (#1921 follow-up) ───────────────────────────────
# Tests used real issue numbers as identity fixtures — 25 of the 29 in use were
# live issues or PRs, and #42 is still OPEN. A run keyed to one of those writes
# fabricated prior work onto that issue's state branch; measured on this repo,
# zbuild/state/issue-999 held 68 commits of test payloads and issue-698 held 121.
# Now that CI chains and pushes (#1970, #2006), that reaches origin.
#
# 9_0000000+ is unreachable: this repo is ~2000 issues in. A stray
# zbuild/state/issue-9xxxxxxx ref is therefore unmistakably test residue, safe to
# reclaim, and can never be confused with someone's work.
# The floor of the reserved range. Read by lint-test-identity and the hygiene
# test; zb_test_issue composes its ids to always land at or above it.
ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR=90000000
export ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR

# Sequential within a test file: 90000001, 90000002, … Files repeat the same ids,
# which is safe because each runs in its own throwaway repo — and if one ever
# escapes, the number identifies it instantly.
# The counter lives in a FILE, not a shell variable: callers use $(zb_test_issue),
# which runs in a subshell, so an in-memory counter would never advance and every
# call would return the same id.
#
# The id is keyed on the PID so two test files running in PARALLEL never mint the
# same one. They otherwise all start at 90000001, and the teardown below deletes
# refs from the SHARED checkout — so one file's cleanup could delete a ref another
# file was still asserting on. The unit tier is parallel by default (#984), and
# more cores make that likelier, which is why it showed on Linux CI first.
#
# Shape: 9 + PID%1000 (3) + seq (4) — always 8 digits, always >= 90000000.
zb_test_issue() {
    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
    local f="$dir/.zb-test-issue-seq"
    local n=0
    [[ -r "$f" ]] && n="$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || printf '0')"
    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
    n=$(( n + 1 ))
    printf '%d' "$n" > "$f" 2>/dev/null || true
    local id
    id="$(printf '9%03d%04d' "$(( $$ % 1000 ))" "$n")"
    # Record it, so teardown removes exactly the refs THIS file minted rather
    # than every reserved ref it happens to find.
    printf '%s\n' "$id" >> "$dir/.zb-test-issue-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
    printf '%s' "$id"
}

# Goal fixtures get the same treatment: the marker makes zbuild/state/goal-<hash>
# traceable back to a test even though the hash itself is opaque.
#
# The hash is RECORDED as it is handed out, exactly as zb_test_issue records ids.
# Without that, goal refs had no teardown and no guard — which is precisely how
# the leak fixed in this branch survived a full identity sweep unnoticed. The
# derivation mirrors zbuild_goal_key: sha256 of the text with all whitespace
# stripped, truncated to 12 hex.
zb_test_goal() {
    local text; text="$(printf '[zb-test] %s' "${1:-fixture}")"
    local dir="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}"
    local h
    h="$(printf '%s' "$text" | tr -d '[:space:]' | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-12)"
    printf '%s\n' "$h" >> "$dir/.zb-test-goal-minted" 2>/dev/null || true
    printf '%s' "$text"
}

# A throwaway repo WITH an origin. setup_git_temp_repo builds the working tree;
# this adds the bare remote a push needs. Promoted out of persist-stage-test.sh,
# where it lived as _mk_repo.
zb_test_repo() {
    local name="${1:-zbrepo}"
    local remote="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name-remote.git"
    local repo
    repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "$name")" || return 1
    local real_git; real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
    (
        "$real_git" init -q --bare "$remote"
        cd "$repo" || exit 1
        "$real_git" remote add origin "$remote"
        "$real_git" push -q -u origin main
    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$repo"
}

# Reserved-range state refs in a repo (default: the real checkout). Used by both
# the teardown below and the suite-wide hygiene guard.
# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # callers live in tests/, which CI's shellcheck step
# does not scan (it covers scripts core plugins), so the optional repo argument
# looks unpassed from inside this file alone.
zb_test_reserved_refs() {
    local repo="${1:-${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}}"
    # Prefix glob, then a NUMERIC filter — not 'issue-9???????'. That counted
    # characters, so it covered 90000000-99999999 only, while lint-test-identity
    # and _cleanup_issue_ref_decision both gate on >= 90000000. An id above the
    # 8-digit range would have passed both and been invisible here.
    local _ref _n
    while IFS= read -r _ref; do
        [[ -n "$_ref" ]] || continue
        _n="${_ref##*/issue-}"
        [[ "$_n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
        # An explicit if, not `[[ … ]] && printf`: the && form returns non-zero
        # when the test is false, and as the last command in the loop body that
        # aborts callers running under `set -e`.
        if [[ "$_n" -ge "${ZB_TEST_ISSUE_FLOOR:-90000000}" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$_ref"
        fi
    done < <(git -C "$repo" for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' \
        'refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-9*' 2>/dev/null || true)
}

cleanup_test_env() {
    # Remove state refs THIS FILE minted and may have written into the real
    # checkout. Deliberately not "every reserved ref present": the unit tier runs
    # in parallel, so deleting another file's in-flight ref would fail its
    # assertions. Reserved-range by construction, so a real issue's branch is
    # never touched — not even one already contaminated.
    local _minted="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}/.zb-test-issue-minted"
    if [[ -n "${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -r "$_minted" ]]; then
        local _id
        while IFS= read -r _id; do
            [[ "$_id" =~ ^9[0-9]{7}$ ]] || continue
            git -C "${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" update-ref -d \
                "refs/heads/zbuild/state/issue-$_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        done < "$_minted"
    fi
    local _gminted="${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}/.zb-test-goal-minted"
    if [[ -n "${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" && -r "$_gminted" ]]; then
        local _h
        while IFS= read -r _h; do
            [[ "$_h" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{12}$ ]] || continue
            git -C "${REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" update-ref -d \
                "refs/heads/zbuild/state/goal-$_h" 2>/dev/null || true
        done < "$_gminted"
    fi

    if [[ -n "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" && -d "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" ]]; then
        rm -rf "$TEST_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    [[ -n "${ORIG_HOME:-}" ]] && export HOME="$ORIG_HOME" || true
    [[ -n "${ORIG_PATH:-}" ]] && export PATH="$ORIG_PATH" || true
    # Restore ZBUILD_STATE_DIR and ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR to pre-setup values
    # (or unset them if they were not set before this test sourced the helpers).
    if [[ -n "${ORIG_STATE_DIR_SET:-}" ]]; then
        export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$ORIG_STATE_DIR"
    else
        unset ZBUILD_STATE_DIR
    fi
    if [[ -n "${ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR_SET:-}" ]]; then
        export ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR="$ORIG_ARTIFACT_DIR"
    else
        unset ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR
    fi
}
